sections.heading: How the calculation works
body: The calculator works out the sun's altitude from your date and latitude/longitude and finds the time ranges where it falls in set bands. Sunrise and sunset are when the top of the sun touches the horizon (altitude about -0.83°). Golden hour runs from that moment up to about +6° altitude, and blue hour covers about -6° up to sunrise (or from just after sunset down to -6°).
Results are listed as morning blue hour, morning golden hour, evening golden hour and evening blue hour. Your location is used only in your browser and is never sent to a server.

sections.heading: Worked examples
list: In Incheon, Korea (latitude 37.4563, longitude 126.7052) on October 2, 2026, morning blue hour is about 06:03 to 06:29 and morning golden hour about 06:29 to 07:03. Evening golden hour is about 17:40 to 18:15 and evening blue hour about 18:15 to 18:41.

In the same place, the evening golden hour on the summer solstice (June 21) runs about 19:18 to 19:57 (about 39 minutes), and on the winter solstice (December 21) about 16:37 to 17:18 (about 41 minutes). The clock times shift a lot with the season, but the length stays similar.
Near the equator in Singapore (October 2, 2026), golden hour is about 27 minutes and blue hour about 21 minutes, shorter than in Incheon, because the sun sets closer to vertically.
In Tromsø, in the Arctic (latitude 69.65°), the sun never sets on June 21 and never rises on December 21, so there is no golden or blue hour, and the calculator shows a note saying so.

sections.heading: When to use it
body: Once you know where and when you will shoot, it helps you set an exact arrival and setup time before sunrise. It also helps you compare which day and time of a trip is best for shooting.

sections.heading: Limits and common mistakes
list: Times are shown in this device's current time zone. If you enter coordinates for another region, the times may not be that place's local time, so account for the time difference.
The calculation reflects only the sun's geometric position. Clouds, haze, atmospheric conditions and terrain such as mountains or buildings can change when the light actually appears.
Golden and blue hour do not have sharp edges; the light changes gradually. Arrive and set up a few minutes before the start time to be safe.
At high latitudes, midsummer midnight sun and midwinter polar night may mean the bands do not occur.
Latitude is positive in the north and negative in the south, and longitude is positive in the east and negative in the west. A wrong sign puts you in a completely different place.

sections.heading: How to use it
list: Drag images in or press Choose images to add up to 20 at once.

sections.heading: Why file size drops
body: JPG and WebP save an image by discarding detail the human eye struggles to notice. The lower the quality value, the more is discarded and the smaller the file becomes. Go too low and blocky patches appear. A value between 70 and 85 usually cuts the size a lot with almost no visible difference.
Reducing the number of pixels is the most reliable method. Phone photos are often more than 4000 pixels wide, but 1600 to 1920 pixels is plenty for a blog or on-screen use.

sections.heading: Photo info (EXIF) and location
body: Because this tool re-saves your photo, camera details and GPS location are removed by default. That default is the safe choice for photos you post on social media or forums.

When saving a JPG as a JPG you can choose to keep everything or remove only the location. The photo is saved already rotated to its visible orientation, so the orientation tag is reset and the embedded preview thumbnail is dropped. Colors are saved in the web standard sRGB.

faq.question: Are my photos uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: No. Everything is processed inside your browser and your photos are not sent anywhere. Processed images disappear when you close the tab, so download the results you need.

faq.question: Will compressing ruin the quality?
faq.answer: At a JPG or WebP quality of about 70 to 85, the difference is hard to see on screen. If you need a smaller file than that, reducing the maximum width usually harms quality less than lowering quality further.

faq.question: Why doesn't my PNG get much smaller?
faq.answer: PNG is a lossless format, so a quality value cannot shrink it. For photos, switch the output format to JPG or WebP, or reduce the maximum width. A transparent PNG saved as JPG gets a white background where it was transparent.

faq.question: I set a target size but the result is larger.
faq.answer: Depending on the photo, even the lowest quality may not reach the target, and a notice appears. Reduce the maximum width or raise the target a little and try again.

faq.question: What happens to location data when I compress?
faq.answer: By default EXIF and GPS are removed. Only when saving a JPG as a JPG can you keep everything or remove only the location. If hiding location is all you need, the EXIF Remover tool also works.

sections.heading: Three ways to set the size
list: Fit within a maximum size: set width and height limits and the photo is shrunk to fit inside them while keeping its proportions. This is the most common choice.
Scale by percentage: change the size relative to the original, such as 50 percent. Handy for shrinking many photos by the same amount.
Set an exact size: forces the photo to the width and height you enter. If the ratio differs the photo is distorted, so use it only when a size is strictly required.

sections.heading: Recommended sizes by use
body: A blog photo 800 to 1200 pixels wide looks sharp on most screens. Anything larger just adds weight and slows the page. On Instagram, 1080×1350 is the portrait standard and 1080×1080 the square standard.

Printing needs both a print size and a resolution. To print A4 (210×297 mm) at 300 dpi you need about 2480×3508 pixels. To check print quality first, use the Print Resolution Calculator alongside this tool.

sections.heading: Many photos at once
body: You can process up to 20 photos with the same settings and download the results as one ZIP. Saved file names include the new size, for example photo-1200x800.jpg, so they stay distinct from the originals. When shrinking, the image is reduced in several steps rather than one jump, which reduces jagged edges.

faq.question: Can I set only the width and keep the proportions?
faq.answer: Yes. In Fit within a maximum size, enter only the width and leave the height at 0. The height is calculated automatically.

faq.question: Does resizing also reduce file size?
faq.answer: Usually by a lot. Halving the width and height leaves a quarter of the pixels, and the file shrinks accordingly. If you need to hit an exact file size, use the Image Compressor.

faq.question: Does enlarging a small photo make it sharper?
faq.answer: No. Enlarging cannot create detail that was never there, so the photo looks blurry. That is why sizes larger than the original are not applied by default.

faq.question: Are my photos uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: No. Everything is processed inside your browser and your photos are not sent anywhere.

faq.question: Is location data removed when I resize?
faq.answer: By default camera info and location are removed. Turning on Keep EXIF carries the info over only when saving a JPG as a JPG. If you do not want to expose your location, leave it off.

sections.heading: Which format should you choose?
list: JPG: the most widely used photo format, opened by almost every program and site. The default choice for submissions and printing.
PNG: lossless and supports transparency. Good for logos, screenshots and text-heavy images, but files are large for photos.
WebP: smaller than JPG at the same quality, so it suits web pages. Some older programs cannot open it.

sections.heading: Converting iPhone HEIC photos
body: By default iPhones save photos in the compact HEIC format. Windows and some shopping or government submission sites cannot read it, so it has to become JPG.
When you choose a HEIC file, it is first decoded to JPG and then saved in the format you picked. If a HEIC file contains several images, only the main one is converted.

sections.heading: What changes during conversion
body: JPG and WebP are lossy, so each conversion costs a little quality. Convert once from the original whenever possible. Turning a transparent PNG into JPG fills the transparent area with white or the color you pick. Converting does not keep EXIF and GPS information.

faq.question: Can I convert iPhone HEIC photos to JPG?

faq.question: Are my photos uploaded to a server?

faq.question: Does converting reduce quality?

faq.question: Are animated GIFs converted?
faq.answer: Only the first frame of an animated GIF is converted. The animation is not kept.

faq.question: Can I convert RAW files?
faq.answer: No. This tool supports JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, AVIF and HEIC. RAW files such as CR3, NEF or ARW are not supported.

ImageMosaic.aboutTitle: How to use the image mosaic tool
ImageMosaic.aboutBody: Photos you post to a blog or community often catch things that should be hidden, such as a passerby's face, a license plate or the address on a delivery label. Drag over the parts you want to hide and choose pixelation, blur or a black box. Your photo is processed inside your browser and never uploaded to a server.
ImageMosaic.disclaimer: Faces are not detected automatically, so you need to mark each area yourself. Check the preview to be sure everything is covered before saving. A weak mosaic can still be readable.

sections.heading: How to use it
list: Choose a photo and the editor appears.
Drag over each part to hide. Add as many areas as you need and use Undo last area to remove a mistake.
Pick the method and strength, and the preview updates right away.
Press Apply mosaic and the result is made at the original resolution with a download link.

sections.heading: Which method is safest?
body: A black box erases the information in that area completely, so it is the most reliable. Use it for license plates, addresses, phone numbers and ID numbers, where text must never be readable.

Pixelate and blur look more natural, but at low strength text or faces may remain recognizable. Cover a generous area and set the strength high, around 7 or more. This tool sizes the mosaic cells relative to the area, so it stays hard to read even on large photos.

sections.heading: Check before you post
body: Personal information in a photo is not only what you can see. The EXIF data can contain location coordinates. By default this tool re-saves the photo and removes EXIF and GPS. Also look again for reflections in windows or sunglasses and for text showing through the back of a document.

faq.question: Does it find faces and hide them automatically?
faq.answer: No. For now you drag to mark each area yourself. This lets the photo stay on your device, and you can see and choose exactly what is hidden.

faq.question: Are my photos uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: No. Everything is processed inside your browser and your photo is not sent anywhere, so it is safe to use with sensitive photos.

faq.question: Can the hidden part be restored later?
faq.answer: The saved result does not keep the original pixels, so it cannot be restored by ordinary means. At low strength the rough shape may still be guessed, so raise the strength or use the black box.

faq.question: How should I hide license plates or addresses?
faq.answer: For information that must not be readable, use the black box. Pixelate and blur can leave text readable unless the strength is high enough.

faq.question: What happens to location data when I save?
faq.answer: By default EXIF and location are removed. Only a JPG saved with Keep EXIF turned on retains the original photo info.
